newsitem.title: UK: Tabloids press for total British handgun ban.
newsitem.headline: Tabloids press for total British handgun ban.

text.p: Britain's two top-selling daily newspapers on Friday urged readers to tell the government they wanted nothing short of a total ban on handguns in the wake of the Dunblane tragedy.
The tabloid Sun and Daily Mirror which between them sell over five million copies a day, printed coupons for readers to clip out, sign and send off to the corridors of power.
"Please, please think again and ban EVERY handgun from civilian possession and use," the Sun's coupon, addressed to Prime Minister John Major, said.
The government on Wednesday proposed a ban on all handguns except .22 firearms of a sort used for target shooting, and said these should have to be kept in specially secured gun clubs.

But the Mirror and Sun insisted that only a complete ban could assure people that there would never be a repetition of the Dunblane massacre, where crazed loner Thomas Hamilton killed 16 children and a teacher before shooting himself.
The Mirror urged readers to gather signatures for its petition with the words: "Do it now - in memory of Dunblane and for the sake of all our children."
Parliament is expected to vote on the government's plan -- which ministers claim would give Britain some of the toughest gun laws in the world -- before Christmas.
Political analysts said unless campaigners for the abolition of handguns can change the minds of legislators, the government compromise solution could well be passed.
But anger over apparent criticism of the parents of the Dunblane victims by a Conservative MP who opposes any major tightening of the law inflamed the debate on Thursday.
Speaking to his BBC local radio station, John Carlisle said: "Some of them have been far too emotional and partly hysterical on what is a very, very important national issue."
The statement enraged legislators on the other side of the argument. "This latest outburst...will appal decent people," said Alex Salmond, leader of the Scottish National Party.

The proposals go beyond the suggestions of Lord Douglas Cullen, a senior judge who conducted an inquiry into the Dunblane tragedy. In his report presented to the government this week, Cullen urged simply that all handguns be kept in gun clubs.
Major, however, knew he risked defeat in in the 651-seat lower House of Commons, where his Conservatives have a majority of just two seats, unless he went much further.
But gun shops and clubs throughout Britain said even the compromise measures which the government proposes would put them out of business and ruin a sport celebrated at the Olympics.
"This is the behaviour of a Third World dictatorship rather than a Western democracy," said Richard Law, secretary of the Shooter's Rights Association of the government's plans.

"For a political point the government is destroying a sport which millions enjoy, yet they will not make a noticeable difference to public safety with these measures," Christopher Reader, the secretary of a rifle and pistol club, argued.
